page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 AWS Graviton2 processor, utilizing the Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz, with 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a compute-focused allocation of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a 1900 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, and network connectivity is rated at a 12 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results indicate balanced multi-core capabilities alongside some single-core limitations. The instance achieves average performance in multi-core stress-ng (48571.1) and Geekbench multi-core (11706.0) tests, as well as average marks in software compilation (26063.0) and ray tracing (27349.0). However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by Geekbench single-core (958.0) and weak single-threaded gzip compression (20.31 GB/sec). Memory bandwidth is strong for small cached blocks at 1894.03 GB/sec, but drops to 173.34 GB/sec for larger uncached blocks, reflecting a weak overall Passmark memory score of 1830.4.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated physical cores offer a high density of compute resources per unit of power and cost compared to traditional x86 architectures, especially when leveraging the local NVMe SSD storage. This hardware profile is appropriate for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from local high-speed storage, such as database operations (Passmark database score of 20441.91), Redis caching (40.61 million SET operations/sec), static web serving (33.11 GB/sec), and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It is less optimal for single-threaded applications or large-scale LLM inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.8xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized instance powered by a 32-core AWS Graviton2 (Neoverse-N1) processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per core) and a 1900 GB local NVMe SSD instance store. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it provides 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks show average multi-core performance, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 11706.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 17314.07, though single-core metrics are weaker. The instance delivers solid database performance, with 40.61 million Redis SET operations per second and 33.11 GB/sec static web serving throughput. This configuration is efficient for multi-threaded, storage-intensive workloads such as databases, web serving, and software compilation, offering a balanced resource-to-cost ratio through its dedicated ARM cores and integrated high-speed local NVMe storage.
